subject: Private cluster design: NVMe zoning, egress ownership & compact node grid
messages:
From: Amit Singh <amit@lockedrack.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.p@lockedrack.com>, procurement@lockedrack.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Private cluster discovery — compact footprint + NVMe zoning

Diego,

Thanks again for the intro call last week. We're moving from evaluation into procurement and need to lock the operational boundaries for an on-prem private cluster in our locked-rack sites. High level asks from LockedRack: small rack footprint (2-6 nodes per site), NVMe-local tiers for model cache, and a clear owner for egress/NAT so we can satisfy SOC-type audit requirements.

Can you share a compact cluster proposal that calls out: node roles (gpu vs infra vs storage-proxy), NVMe zoning (local cache vs persistent blockstore), how egress routing & NAT ownership should be handled when we colocate with our existing WAN appliances, and any constraints around multi-tenant eviction/priority?

We're hoping to finalize architecture by the 20th so procurement can finish the quote. I've attached our inventory CSV.

Attachment: site-inventory.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Amit Singh
Head of Edge Infrastructure
LockedRack Systems
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Singh <amit@lockedrack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private cluster discovery — compact footprint + NVMe zoning

Amit — thanks for the inventory. See a short proposal attached and a few clarifying bullets below; Marissa and Irene are looped for the technical parts.

Summary bullets:
- Node mix for a 2–6 node rack: 1-2 GPU inference nodes (A450/A100 equivalent), 1 infra node (control plane + proxy), 1 storage-proxy node when persistent blockstore required. For 2-node minimal sites we recommend egress via a regional gateway (see NAT options).
- NVMe zoning: local NVMe on GPU nodes for KV cache / model working set (ephemeral, hot); dedicated encrypted blockstore (iSCSI or local sealed NVMe) on storage-proxy for small persistent shards. We avoid local-only persistent data on GPU nodes to simplify eviction.
- Egress/NAT: customer-owned egress preferred. For LockedRack we recommend: primary egress ownership by LockedRack WAN appliance (preferred) with our fallback via a regional NAT tunnel (Redwood-managed) for failover. This keeps audit trails and KMS in customer control while providing an SLA fallback.
- Multi-tenant eviction/priority: use node labels + QoS + pod priority classes; critical inference pods pin to NVMe-local; best-effort can be preempted. We propose a policy doc to tie priorities to SLOs.

Attachments: nvme-zoning-draft.png (image), lockedrack-compact-cluster-proposal.pdf (pdf)

Next steps: Marissa — can you validate the blockstore sizing and R/W profile assumptions? Irene — confirm network egress flow and what we need for iptables/conntrack tuning. Neha — flag any compliance evidence items that LockedRack will need for procurement.

Diego
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Amit Singh <amit@lockedrack.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private cluster discovery — compact footprint + NVMe zoning

Diego — quick technical review / clarifications. Quoting your bullets inline: 

> Node mix for a 2–6 node rack: 1-2 GPU inference nodes, 1 infra node, 1 storage-proxy node

If LockedRack insists on 2-node minimal footprint, the infra+storage-proxy functions should be colocated on a single M-class server with redundant NICs (bonded). For anything >=4 nodes, split infra from storage-proxy to avoid IO interference.

> NVMe zoning: local NVMe on GPU nodes for KV cache; dedicated encrypted blockstore on storage-proxy

Agree. Important operational note: local NVMe on GPU nodes must be mounted with noatime and tuned for 4k random writes if we expect frequent tokenization/cache churn. Also set eviction thresholds at 70% to avoid sudden GC pauses. Provide example cgroup/limit knobs in the runbook.

> Egress/NAT: customer-owned egress preferred; Redwood-managed NAT tunnel fallback

Operationally we need to ensure consistent source-IP for audit trails. If LockedRack's WAN appliance performs SNAT, we'll need a small egress-proxy on the infra node that stamps an internal request id and forwards to the WAN appliance so logs unify. Also call out conntrack sizing if throughput > 10k conn/s.

I'll draft the runbook snippets and include recommended sysctl tuning and a sample eviction policy.

Marissa
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Amit Singh <amit@lockedrack.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, procurement@lockedrack.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private cluster discovery — compact footprint + NVMe zoning

Thanks — this reads well and addresses most questions. A few answers from our side: 
- For 2-node sites we accept the colocated infra+storage approach for now; our procurement prefers the smallest BOM possible.
- We'll keep primary egress on our WAN appliance; can Redwood provide the egress-proxy image and a sample config so our security team can review the logs format?
- Expected workload per site: median 400 qps, 99p 2.5k qps bursts, mostly small prompt sizes (avg seq length ~300 tokens).

We'll approve the proposal pending the runbook snippets and the sample egress-proxy. Procurement copied here to start contract details.

—Amit

I'll include the compact BOM in a separate note for procurement. If those timelines work, procurement can circulate the SOW and we'll target first pilot site in early Jan.

Diego

Redwood Inference
